task: Vantridge 2025 research tax claim: cost line classification, credit, and election analysis

overall_task_success.commentary: This was a thorough pass that held up on nearly everything I checked. Every headline figure matched what I worked out independently, and it correctly kept a historical balance's original foreign label separate from the current year's domestic treatment of that same location, exactly the distinction that trips this kind of claim up. It caught a genuine ambiguity in the target database and verified before writing. Set against that, one cost line with missing documentation got marked and cited with confidence instead of flagged, its own verification checked totals rather than individual calls, and both the post and the covering note run longer and more formatted than the task called for. Real work, with real gaps once checked closely.

task_accuracy.commentary: Every figure I rebuilt from the source schedules matched what came back here: the reduction, the credit base, both election dates and their recovery amounts, and the foreign amortisation figure broken down by contributing prior year balance. It also handled the one trap that catches this kind of claim out, keeping a historical balance's foreign label distinct from the same location's domestic treatment for current year work under the newer rule. The one thing that slips past that scrutiny is a test engineering line with no source record showing it as wages, supplies, or contract research, where the register still marked it not qualifying and cited specific rules without flagging that the documentation itself was missing.

efficiency.wrong_actions_recovery: one minor detour, it pulled up a formatting reference page partway through that it never ended up needing for the actual deliverable.
efficiency.commentary: This reached a finished, reconciled deliverable quickly, well inside what a job spanning four connected systems and three dozen cost lines should reasonably take, with no thrash and no repeated steps. One real detour sits partway through, a formatting reference page it opened and never used for anything in the final register, post, or draft. The register rows themselves were committed in one continuous write with no midpoint check, so an error anywhere in that batch would only have come to light at the very end rather than while a smaller piece of it was still open. Neither issue is large alone, but together they keep this off a 6.

writing_quality.commentary: The content is accurate and easy to follow, and the reasoning behind each figure holds together well. Two things hold this back from a higher mark. The channel post leans heavily on bold headers and bulleted bands that read more like a formatted internal memo than a message meant to be scanned quickly in a team channel, and it restates the same figures once in a short bulleted summary and then again in the paragraph underneath, adding length without adding new information. The covering note carries a smaller version of the same habit. None of this makes the writing hard to follow, it is simply heavier and more formal than the format called for.

instruction_following.commentary: Every literal piece of the request is here: five specific figures in the channel post, both elections dated precisely, the register's treatment labels matched the exact wording it was given rather than a close paraphrase, and the draft correctly left the recipient field empty with the required warning on its face. The one place this drifts from the letter of the ask is length and register. The brief called for a post and a draft, and what landed reads more like a formatted report in both cases, which is a real gap between what the format was supposed to be and what actually got delivered even though every individual requirement inside that format is satisfied.

collaboration_autonomy_verification.steering_needed: none, it only paused once for the required approval before the channel post went live.
collaboration_autonomy_verification.additional_editing: none beyond adding a verified billing address for the controller before the draft goes out.
collaboration_autonomy_verification.commentary: Two databases shared the exact same register name, a real ambiguity, and it checked both before choosing where to write instead of guessing, exactly the kind of judgment call I want handled without my input. It also caught and correctly named the historical versus current year classification trap a less careful pass would have missed. Its own readback only confirmed the register held the full line count with correct totals, never confirming any individual call was still right, so a wrong row would have passed the same check that cleared everything else. I would also want confirmation the register it wrote to surfaces first for the controller's team, since a duplicate database is still sitting in that workspace.

citation_quality.commentary: The rule trail behind each figure held up when I checked it, tracing to a specific rule and a specific row every time. The foreign amortisation total is broken down into each contributing prior year balance by name rather than one unexplained number, letting me rebuild it and confirm it matched. It also correctly separates a balance's original classification from the current year's schedule rather than blurring the two together. Two things still cost a reader time. The credit base total is broken into its three category totals without matching each to its specific paragraph of the credit rule, and several rows bundle three or four rule citations onto one line without showing the math.

gui_action_correctness.commentary: Not applicable. This ran through the connected systems directly, so there was no on screen click path here to rate either.
